summary: The claim is proved by the final two-case argument. The area and containment reductions are correct, and the cap formulas and breakpoint orderings are consistent. Since P lies in x <= 0, its x-nonnegative part has zero area and Q contributes exactly 1/10 there. If A >= 0, all of P lies in y >= 0, contradicting the prescribed y total. If A < 0, containment forces F > 0, so Q is covered by the x- and y-nonnegative halfspaces, whose Q-areas sum to at most 1/5, contradicting |Q| = 1/3. The cases are exhaustive, including boundary and degenerate endpoint positions allowed by the statement.
